title: You don’t have a “struggle.”
paragraphs: You have a choice you keep postponing.
And deep down… you already know what it is.

You scroll.
You pray—half-hearted.
You promise God, “Tomorrow, I’ll fix this.”

And your silence?
Your delay?
Your “I’m still figuring it out”?
Joshua didn’t give Israel a soft sermon.
He dropped a blade into their comfort:
“Choose this day whom you will serve…” (Joshua 24:15)

Not when you’re ready.
Not when it’s convenient.
Not when the addiction weakens.
And here’s the part we don’t say out loud—

You can sing worship songs
and still be bowing to something else.

You can lift your hands on Sunday
and surrender your body to sin on Monday.

You can say “God is first”
while secretly protecting what He asked you to kill.

You will love one.
You will cling to one.
You will obey one.

So the question is not:
“Do I believe in God?”

The question is:
Who is actually ruling my life right now?

Tired of hiding.
Tired of pretending.
Tired of fighting secret sin that keeps winning in the dark.

You delete the history.
You justify the compromise.
You rename it “weakness” instead of calling it what it is—

“You’ve gone too far.”
“You can’t come back from this.”
“Just stay here.”

Because Joshua’s call to choose…
is not a call to impress God.
It’s a call to stop running from Him.
Joshua stood before a people already rescued.

God had already brought them out of Egypt.
Already split seas.
Already fed them in the wilderness.
And it’s the same for you.
God is not waiting for you to clean yourself up.
He is calling you to come home.
Left to ourselves, we don’t choose God.
We trade glory for cheap substitutes.
“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way.” (Isaiah 53:6)
A heart that chooses everything but God.
“For the wages of sin is death…” (Romans 6:23)
That’s why your sin never satisfies you.
but leaves you emptier every time.
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 6:23)
So Jesus came and chose the cross for you.

He stepped into your failure.
He carried your shame.
He bore the full weight of your rebellion.
“God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Not when you fixed your life.
While you were still in it.
On the cross, Jesus didn’t just forgive sin—

He took the penalty you deserved
so you could receive the life you never earned.

Proving sin doesn’t get the final word.
Shame doesn’t get the final word.
Your past doesn’t get the final word.

Turn from the sin you’ve been protecting.
Bring it into the light.
Stop negotiating with what is killing you.
Because grace is not permission to stay stuck.
It is power to be free.
“If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” (John 8:36)

Not halfway free.
Not someday free.
But you still have to choose.
So let me ask you, heart to heart—

What are you still holding onto
that is keeping you from fully choosing Jesus?
What altar have you refused to tear down?

What sin have you renamed
so you don’t have to crucify it?

Even if your voice shakes.
Even if your past screams.
Even if you feel unworthy.

“Jesus, I’m done running.”
“I give You everything.”
“Be Lord over my life.”
And watch what He does with a surrendered heart.

He restores.
He renews.
He rebuilds.
He doesn’t just forgive your past—
If this hit something deep in you—
Let this be your moment of decision.
